transcript.dialogue: I'm Mira. Careful with the table, the ink is still wet from the morning shift. Do you usually track clay all the way up your elbows, or is today special?
Just a normal Tuesday at the wheel, I'm afraid. It washes off. Mostly.
A normal Tuesday is brave. Most people I know try to pretend Tuesdays don't even exist. Do you work upside down when you're throwing clay, or are you strictly a right-side-up potter?
Strictly right-side-up these days. Though I used to do things the hard way for a living. You mapmaker? I noticed the compass.
Only on Tuesdays, strictly speaking. If you flip the street grid upside down, the old bakery on 4th becomes a shortcut to nowhere.
A shortcut to nowhere sounds like a lot of extra walking. I usually prefer places where you stay put.
Staying put is fine until the ground moves, but a little wandering keeps the legs limber. You look like a man who knows where every heavy thing in the room is.
transcript.action: sketch a tiny arrow on the napkin

transcript.dialogue: I do. Spent twenty years making sure I wouldn't trip on anything sharp. It was really nice talking to you tonight.
It was really nice talking to you too, Dex. If you ever need a map for a place that only stays still, you know who to ask.
Take care out there, Mira. See you around.

transcript.dialogue: I'm Mira. Careful with the table, the ink is still wet from the morning shift. Did you come straight from a studio or is today just unusually messy?
Neither, I've just got clumsy hands today. What kind of compass is that on your chain?
It's just an old brass pocket one, mostly for checking if my desk is level. Do you ever look at a blueprint or a map and just want to turn it sideways to see what happens?
Only if the map's got a grid on it, otherwise everything gets lost. What kind of desk needs a level anyway?
Just an old drafting table that likes to lean toward the harbor.
A drafting table leaning toward the harbor sounds damp. Why don't ghosts haunt lighthouses? Because the stairs are too loud.
That's a very dry one for a damp table. I think I'll pass on the dare tonight, Nell.
Suit yourself, Mira. Some jokes just don't have the structural integrity to hold up under weather.
I have to be up early to ink the transit grids anyway. Take care of those notes in your pockets.
I should probably head home and feed the cat. Have a safe walk.

transcript.dialogue: Good to see you again, Dex. At least these two aren't asking for a seating chart yet.
Good to see you too, Mira. Glad the ink made it off your fingers this time.

Honestly, I'd take a seating chart over hearing about their matching workout routines one more time. Have you ever tried doing the opposite of whatever a GPS tells you just to see where it spits you out?
transcript.action: taps compass against the salt shaker

transcript.dialogue: Not since about nineteen-ninety-eight. Usually ended up in a ditch or a farmer's turnip patch. Though I suppose that counts as a thrill, if you're looking for one.
A turnip patch sounds like better company than whoever's running that midnight wrap party anyway. Which way is north from here?
North is wherever the salt shaker isn't. Thanks for not running off to the party.
If north is the salt shaker, we're currently heading straight into the water pitcher. You read that upside down without even blinking.
Well, that's my specialty. Turning things upside down. Would you want to grab actual quiet coffee tomorrow? Just the two of us.
Tomorrow sounds perfect. Let's take the long way around the block so we don't hit the main drag.
Sounds like a plan. A very long, very slow walk.
